description_full: Matrix IT Ltd., together with its subsidiaries, provides information technology (IT) solutions and services in Israel, the United States, and Europe. It operates in four segments: Information Technology Solutions and Services, Consulting, and Management in Israel; Information Technology Solutions and Services in the United States; Sale, Marketing, and Support of Software Products; and Cloud and Computing Infrastructures. The company offers customer experience, customer relationship management, enterprise resource planning Tafnit and Priority, call centers, warehouse management system, 3D printing, and matrix open hub; testing and automation, nearshore and offshore services, training and implementation, and DevOps; software representation; and cyber security, regulations and compliance, business continuity management, and disaster recovery solutions. It also provides data solutions, including AI, big data and analytics, databricks COE, hyper automation, cognitive document extraction, and deep learning research; digital and mobile solutions; and cloud, ITaaS, data and integration platforms, infrastructure, modernization, low code, and networks solutions. In addition, the company offers consulting services, such as customer facing, business excellence, defense consulting, urban planning and environment, infrastructure and transport, healthcare consulting, supply chain management, trend and technology spotting, and technology for finance, as well as engineering consulting and project management services. It serves the banking and finance, high-tech and startups, government and the public sector, security/defense, transportation, health, industry, retail and trade, and education and academia industries. The company exports its products. Matrix IT Ltd. was incorporated in 1989 and is headquartered in Herzliya, Israel.

financial_summary: MATRIX IT LTD. is a mid-cap technology business with a $3.1B market cap.
The top line has compounded at +17% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 14% against a 8% cost of capital, a 6-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it, with gross margins sitting at 36%.
The business throws off $36M in free cash flow, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.29× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.7%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 48% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is.
